成功返回 `{"status":"ok","results":[{"actions":[...],"units":...},...],"units":...}`，结果与请求顺序相同，顶层 units 是全部成功项的动作单位之和。失败整批返回 `{"status":"error","error":"错误码","requestIndex":序号,"results":[],"units":0}`，序号从 0 开始。顶层结构非法用 invalid-batch 和 null 序号，批内元素结构非法用 invalid-batch-item 和实际序号。逐项处理，首个失败项的实际错误码结束整批，无部分结果。预算仍须是非负整数，G2 的单项回退不受发布配额限制。

TEST-REPORT.md.text:
# Test report — unit K01 (G3 batch rollback)

Last run: 2026-11-13, Python 3.12.10, Windows. Command:

```
python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v
```

## Result

| Suite | Tests | Passed | Failed | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/test_compat.py` (G1+G2) | 30 | 30 | 0 | Green **before** the G3 change too (see Baseline) |
| `tests/test_batch.py` (G3) | 29 | 29 | 0 | Written from SPEC before implementation |
| **Total** | **59** | **59** | **0** | |

Also run: `python baseline.py` — all 16 legacy single-request probes return
byte-identical output to the pre-change capture. The only changed line is
`rollback-many`, which previously returned `unsupported-action` and now returns
`invalid-batch` for an empty `requests` array.

## Baseline (captured before any edit)

Probe results for G1/G2 behavior, recorded before implementation and re-verified
after. All matched:

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| staging plan, b<-a, budget 10 | `ok [a,b] units 3` |
| staging plan, 2 changes × 2 units | `budget-exceeded` |
| production plan, `changes:"bad"` | `production-frozen` |
| production rollback, `changes:"bad"` | `production-frozen` |
| rollback applied, no retain | `ok [b,a] units 5` |
| rollback applied, retain [b] | `ok [] units 0` |
| rollback retain [z] (not applied) | `invalid-retain` |
| `changes` not a list | `invalid-change` |
| unknown action | `unsupported-action` |
| unknown environment | `invalid-environment` |
| `budget: true` | `invalid-budget` |
| conflicting duplicate IDs | `conflicting-change` |
| dangling dependency | `unknown-dependency` |
| 2-node cycle | `dependency-cycle` |
| `rollback-many` (pre-G3) | `unsupported-action` → now `invalid-batch` |
| non-object request | `invalid-request` |
| unparseable JSON | `invalid-json` |

## Important pre-existing behavior (not bugs — do not "fix")

- A staging **plan** is capped at 3 units even when `budget` is larger (G2 §2),
  so plans with ≥4 units legitimately return `budget-exceeded`. Several tests
  observe ordering through **rollback** instead, because rollback is uncapped.
- `changes` absent or JSON `null` is `invalid-change` (the key is required).
- `retain` is only consulted for rollback; on plan it is ignored entirely.
- `retain` given as a non-list (including `null`) is `invalid-retain`, not
  `invalid-change` (G2 §3 rejects *malformed* retain lists there).
- An item key outside the allowed five is `invalid-batch-item`, but a **known**
  key with a bad value is a business error from the normal validators.

## G3 behaviors verified

Envelope: only two top-level fields; `requests` must be a list of 1..128;
128 items accepted. Items: must be objects with a subset of
`environment/budget/changes/applied/retain` (no `action`); `rollback-many`
pins each to rollback so the staging plan cap never applies.

Results: exact `{"actions":[...],"units":n}` per item, request order, top-level
`units` is the sum. Failures: `{"status":"error","error":..,"requestIndex":i,
"results":[],"units":0}`, `null` index for envelope errors, real index for item
errors, first failure ends the batch with no partial results. Every G2 business
code is preserved per item (`production-frozen`, `invalid-budget`,
`invalid-environment`, `invalid-change`, `unknown-dependency`,
`conflicting-change`, `invalid-retain`); structure errors outrank business
errors for the same item.

Independence: two items reusing the same IDs/applied sets produce identical
results; one item's `retain` does not affect the next.

Transitive retain through unapplied intermediates: `c(applied) -> b(unapplied)
-> a(applied)` with `retain:["c"]` keeps `a`.

Scale: 1 × 2,000 changes with unapplied intermediates < 10 s; 128 × 2,000
changes < 60 s (measured 0.25 s). A 5,000-node chain and a 2,000-wide diamond
were also probed manually: iterative walks, no recursion error.

## Unfinished / out of scope

- **One intentional behavior change outside the batch path**: `retained_closure`
  now walks through unapplied nodes, so a single rollback with
  `c(applied) -> b(unapplied) -> a(applied)`, `retain:["c"]` keeps `a` where the
  previous code rolled `a` back. This follows G3 §28 (trace the full graph, then
  exclude only applied ancestors) and G2 §3 ("transitive dependencies"), and is
  covered by `BatchSemanticsTest.test_transitive_dependencies_through_unapplied_intermediates`.
- **`budget-exceeded` is unreachable inside a batch by design.** SPEC G3 says
  item rollback is not capped by the release quota, and rollback has no other
  ceiling, so a batch item can only fail budget validation (`invalid-budget`),
  never exceed it. If a later goal adds a rollback cap, add a batch test for it.
- The `retain`-through-unapplied rule was implemented to the G3 wording ("trace
  the full graph, then exclude only applied ancestors"); no separate
  G2-only reading is verified because G3 supersedes it for batch and single
  rollback now shares that code path.
- No property-based/fuzz testing; inputs are hand-written from SPEC.
- No performance test for pathological graphs with very high fan-out beyond the
  2,000-wide diamond probe.

policy.py.text:
"""Validate release policy before computing actions.

Policy owns three decisions and nothing else: whether the requested
environment/action pair may run at all, how the budget constrains a plan, and
the maximum staging plan budget. It is a leaf module -- it imports nothing from
the project -- so planner.py can depend on it without a cycle.
"""

ENVIRONMENTS = {"staging", "production"}
ACTIONS = {"plan", "rollback"}

# G2: this release is staging only. Both operations are frozen for production,
# and the freeze is decided here so it is reported before any graph or change
# validation (a malformed graph in production still reports production-frozen).
FROZEN_ENVIRONMENTS = {"production"}

# G2: the staging plan limit. A staging plan never emits more than this many
# units, regardless of how large `budget` is.
STAGING_PLAN_LIMIT = 3


class PolicyError(ValueError):
    pass


class Decision:
    """Request-level facts policy decides; the planner consumes them read-only."""

    __slots__ = ("action", "budget", "limit")

    def __init__(self, action, budget, limit):
        self.action = action
        # The request budget, as supplied.
        self.budget = budget
        # The effective plan ceiling: the smaller of the request budget and the
        # staging plan limit. Only plan is capped; rollback gets no ceiling
        # because capping it would leave the environment half-reverted.
        self.limit = limit


def limit_for(request, action=None):
    """Validate environment, action and budget; return a Decision.

    `action` overrides the request's own `action` field. Planner uses this for
    G3 batch items, whose action is pinned to "rollback" by the batch entry and
    must never be read from the item itself. When omitted (single requests) the
    request field is read exactly as before.

    The budget is validated for every action, but `limit` is only compared for
    plan (see planner._plan_one).
    """
    environment = request.get("environment")
    if not isinstance(environment, str) or environment not in ENVIRONMENTS:
        raise PolicyError("invalid-environment")
    if environment in FROZEN_ENVIRONMENTS:
        # Checked before the action: an unknown action in production is still a
        # frozen production request, and the freeze is the more useful answer.
        raise PolicyError("production-frozen")
    if action is None:
        action = request.get("action")
    if not isinstance(action, str) or action not in ACTIONS:
        raise PolicyError("unsupported-action")
    budget = request.get("budget")
    # type() rather than isinstance() so booleans never count as a budget.
    if type(budget) is not int or budget < 0:
        raise PolicyError("invalid-budget")
    if action == "plan":
        return Decision(action, budget, min(budget, STAGING_PLAN_LIMIT))
    return Decision(action, budget, None)

ARCHITECTURE.md.text:
# Release planner — architecture handoff (unit K02, G4)

Read this first, then `SPEC.md` (the contract) **together with** `CHANGE-G2.md`
(the G4 owner revision, which wins where the two disagree), then `PLAN-K02.md`
(what K02 changed and why), then run `python -m unittest -v`.

If you are the next session: read §1–§5 before touching code, §8 before
changing anything in the batch path, and §9 before assuming a test expectation
is a spec requirement.

## 1. What this program is

A local Python 3.11+ (developed and verified on 3.12) planning service. One
JSON request on stdin via `python release.py`, one JSON object on stdout,
process exits 0 for every input including malformed ones. No files are created,
no network is touched, nothing is deployed. Import of any module performs no I/O.

## 2. Module responsibilities and dependency direction

```
release.py  (transport only)
    |
    v
planner.py  (orchestration: batch replay/quota + graph/order + result assembly)
   /      \
  v        v
journal.py  policy.py      (both leaves: import only the stdlib)
```

| Module | Owns | Must not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `release.py` | stdin JSON decode, `invalid-json`, printing, exit code | contain validation or plan logic |
| `policy.py` | environment, action, budget; production freeze; staging plan cap (`3`); G4 batch `limit` field validation | import any project module or graph/journal data |
| `journal.py` | request-boundary validation of changes / `applied` / `retain` / `operation_id`; change dedupe vs. conflict; G4 operation fingerprint | build the graph, order changes, or know about batch results |
| `planner.py` | batch envelope, G4 ordered replay + quota, graph build, cycle detection, topological order, rollback selection, result shapes | decode stdin or parse raw JSON text |

Imports always point **inward toward the leaves** (`release -> planner ->
{journal, policy}`). `journal` and `policy` never import `planner`, so there
is no cycle. Only the standard library is used (`heapq`, `json`).

No new module was added in G3 or G4 (SPEC: "Keep these four modules"), and
`release.py` is untouched since K01 — dispatch happens inside `plan()`, so the
transport contract is identical for single and batch requests.

## 3. Request flow (single request, unchanged by G3/G4)

1. `release.main` decodes JSON. Bad JSON -> `invalid-json` with the legacy
   top-level error shape.
2. `planner.plan` checks `request` is an object (`invalid-request`), then
   dispatches: a request carrying `requests` (or `action == "rollback-many"`)
   -> `plan_batch`, otherwise the single-item path.
3. Single path, in this exact order — **the order is observable and part of the
   contract**:
   1. `policy.limit_for` — environment, then production freeze, then action,
      then budget. This is why a malformed graph in `production` still reports
      `production-frozen` (G2 §1).
   2. `journal.read_changes` — validates records, collapses identical
      duplicates, rejects conflicting IDs, sorts by ID.
   3. `journal.read_applied` — validates the persisted journal.
   4. `planner.build_graph` — dangling dependency targets -> `unknown-dependency`.
   5. applied IDs not present in the graph -> `unknown-dependency`.
   6. `planner.topological_order` — over **all** changes -> `dependency-cycle`.
   7. `rollback`: `journal.read_retain` -> `invalid-retain`, then
      `rollback_actions`. `plan`: filter unapplied, compare emitted units with
      the effective limit -> `budget-exceeded`.
   8. Success object, with `units` counted from the **emitted** actions.

Single requests ignore `operation_id` and `limit` (extra keys are never read),
so nothing in the batch interface can change single-request behavior.
Per item, a batch runs this same path (step 3 inside `_compute_item`).

## 4. Batch (`rollback-many`) flow — G4

Envelope (`action`, `limit`, `requests`; exactly three top-level fields):

- `limit` is **required** and must be a nonnegative integer (`type() is int`);
  booleans, floats, strings, null and a missing key are `invalid-batch` with
  `requestIndex: null`. It is validated in `policy.batch_limit` but reported
  through the batch error shape, because no single request has a batch quota.
- `requests` is a list of 1..128 items, checked before any item.
- A top-level `environment` is **not** allowed any more (G3 tolerated and
  silently ignored it). The batch environment is per item.

Per item, in request order (`plan_batch`):

1. `_check_item`: must be an object whose keys are a subset of
   `operation_id, environment, budget, changes, applied, retain`; `operation_id`
   must be a nonempty string of at most 64 characters. Otherwise
   `invalid-batch-item` with the item's real index. Only the operation id and
   the key set are inspected — no request data.
2. Retry / conflict against the **first** item seen with that `operation_id`:
   same id and equivalent request data -> retry (the first result stands, at
   its first position, billed once); same id, different data ->
   `conflicting-operation` with the index of this **later** item.
3. Only for a new id: `_compute_item` -> `_plan_one(item, "rollback")`, i.e.
   every G2 rule applies unchanged and errors keep their own code and index.
   A retry is never revalidated.
4. After every item completed: `sum(result.units) > limit` ->
   `batch-limit-exceeded` with a null index. Equality is allowed.

Success: `{"status":"ok","results":[{"operationId":..,"actions":[..],"units":n},...],
"units":N}` in request order; `N` is the sum over **deduplicated** items.
Error: `{"status":"error","error":code,"requestIndex":i|null,"results":[],
"units":0}`. Batch errors carry `results`, never `actions`. No partial results.

"Equivalent request data" = the item minus `operation_id`, compared as JSON
structure: object key order ignored, array order kept, number != boolean,
and the documented empty defaults (`depends_on`, `applied`, `retain`) equal to
an explicit `[]`. See `journal.operation_fingerprint` and `PLAN-K02.md` §4.

## 5. Design decisions you must not "clean up"

- **Replay accounting**: `units` is always recomputed from emitted actions, not
  from the request. Applied changes satisfy dependencies but never contribute
  units. G4 billing: one unit sum per **unique** operation, retries are free.
- **Determinism**: Kahn's algorithm with a min-heap of IDs, so ties among
  currently eligible changes break lexicographically. Rollback is the reverse of
  that single full order. The order is computed over the whole graph *before*
  filtering, so a cycle behind an applied node is still detected.
- **Retained closure through unapplied nodes** (`retained_closure`): walks all
  dependency edges, keeps only applied nodes. `c -> b(unapplied) -> a(applied)`
  keeps `a` when `c` is retained. Iterative on purpose (2,000+ chains).
- **Two-phase G4 border**: `_check_item` (structure/id, no data) is separate
  from `_compute_item` (G2 + compute) so that duplicate/conflict is judged on
  *identity* before validity, and so the first real failure outranks the quota.
- **One ordered pass, not "validate all then compute all"**: a conflict is only
  knowable per item, in order (§4). `plan_batch` returns at the first failure.
- **Retries are not recomputed**: re-running a retry would risk a different
  answer for identical input and would double-bill by construction.
- **`type(x) is int`** everywhere a count/budget/limit is read, so JSON
  `true`/`false` are never silently treated as 1/0.
- **Fingerprint tags** (`_canonical`, `_ordered_unique`): markers are list-first
  and every JSON node becomes a tagged tuple with a one-character tag, so no
  JSON value can forge one; `1`, `1.0`, `true` get separate tags; the
  unknown-type fallback is type-tagged (`"o", type().__name__, repr`) so an
  in-process exotic value cannot alias a real string.
- **Fast retry path** in `plan_batch`: the *same object* re-sent is skipped
  without re-fingerprinting. It is identity-based (`is`), never `==`, because
  Python says `1 == True`. It is an optimization only; the fingerprint decides.

## 6. Implementation order (what was done; follow this next time)

1. Read `CHANGE-G2.md` G4, then `SPEC.md`, then probe the current CLI on the
   edges the revision touches. Record the probes before editing anything.
2. Write the new contract tests (`tests/test_g4_batch.py`) from the revision
   text. They must fail first.
3. Adapt the helper layer (`tests/support.py`) — every suite shares it.
4. Implement in leaves-to-orchestrator order: `journal` (validation,
   fingerprint) -> `policy` (`limit`) -> `planner` (envelope, item check,
   loop, quota). `release.py` never changes.
5. Re-run all suites and `baseline.py`; recapture the baseline lines the
   revision intentionally moved, noting the old value in the file.
6. Update `PLAN-K02.md`, this file, `TEST-REPORT.md`, `PROJECT-GOAL.md`.

## 7. Verification method

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v` — 101 tests (K02).
- `python baseline.py` — 20 recorded CLI probes; non-zero exit on any drift.
  This is the fastest "did I break single-request behavior" check.
- Scale (all measured on the K02 machine, Python 3.12.10, Windows):
  1 item × 2,000 changes with unapplied intermediates ~0.02 s;
  128 unique items × 2,000 changes ~1.7 s (limit 60 s);
  128 retries of one 2,000-change operation ~0 s in-process, ~1.8 s through
  the CLI including JSON parsing of a 19.8 MB payload.
- Manual smoke:
  `echo '{"action":"rollback-many","limit":5,"requests":[{"operation_id":"a",
  "environment":"staging","budget":0,"changes":[],"applied":[]}]}' | python release.py`
  -> one compact JSON line, exit 0.

## 8. What is deliberately NOT a rule (do not "fix" these)

- `budget-exceeded` is unreachable for single rollback and for batch items:
  rollback is uncapped (G2/G4), and the only rollback ceiling is the batch
  `limit`. Hits are `batch-limit-exceeded` with a null index.
- A staging `plan` is capped at 3 units even with a larger `budget` (G2 §2),
  so plans with >= 4 units legitimately fail. Tests observe ordering through
  rollback for that reason.
- `changes` absent or null is `invalid-change`; `retain` absent defaults to `[]`
  but `retain: null` is `invalid-retain`; `retain` is ignored on `plan`.
- An item key outside the allowed six is `invalid-batch-item`, but a known key
  with a bad value is a business error from the normal validators.
- A retry whose request data would fail G2 is never revalidated; the failure
  (if any) was already raised by its first occurrence. Two *identical* malformed
  retries therefore report one error, not two.
- Item-order of the identity check: for a repeated id, `conflicting-operation`
  is raised before that item's G2 validation could have run.

## 9. Rollback order (if G4 must be withdrawn to G3)

Undo in reverse dependency order. Only the batch path changed in K02, except
`journal.py`'s new helpers (batch-only) and `policy.batch_limit` (batch-only).

1. `planner.py`: restore the K01 `plan_batch`/`_check_envelope`
   (`BATCH_TOP_FIELDS = {"action","requests"}`, `BATCH_ITEM_FIELDS` without
   `operation_id`, per-item `_plan_one` loop, results without `operationId`).
   Delete `_check_item`, `_compute_item`, the `seen` ledger and the quota block.
2. `policy.py`: delete `batch_limit`.
3. `journal.py`: delete `read_operation_id`, `operation_fingerprint`,
   `_canonical`, `_ordered_unique`, `OPERATION_ID_MAX`. (Nothing else uses them.)
4. Tests: delete `tests/test_g4_batch.py`; in `tests/test_batch.py` drop
   `operation_id`/`limit`/`operationId` from the assertions; in
   `tests/support.py` restore `batch(requests, **extra)` and delete `item()`.
5. `baseline.py`: restore the single G3 batch line
   (`{"action":"rollback-many","requests":[]}`) and delete the G4 lines; the
   two G1..G2 batch-adjacent lines above it keep their recorded values.
6. Docs: `PLAN-K02.md` gets a withdrawal banner, this file drops §4/§5's G4
   parts, `TEST-REPORT.md` records the revert run.
7. **Not** to be reverted with G4: the G3 `retained_closure` fix (walking
   through unapplied nodes). It is intended behavior and is covered by
   `tests/test_compat.py::test_retain_traces_through_unapplied_intermediates`.

CHANGE-G2.md.text:
# 发布规划器 G4 业主修订

升级批量回退，原单项接口和 G2 行为全部继续有效。批量接口现在只允许 action、limit、requests 三个顶层字段。limit 为非负整数，布尔值无效。批内每项额外必填 operation_id，为非空字符串，最多 64 个字符，逐字精确比较。

同一批内，operation_id 相同且完整请求数据相同的后续项只视为重试。仅返回第一次的结果，计费一次。对象字段顺序不影响等价，数组顺序保留，JSON 数字和布尔值不能混同。ID 相同但请求数据不同，报 conflicting-operation，序号指向发生冲突的后续项。不同 operation_id 彼此独立，即使回退参数完全一样。有效结果中每项新增 operationId 字段，取请求的 operation_id。

按原请求顺序处理。先校验单项结构和操作 ID，然后判断重复或冲突。仅新 ID 执行该项的 G2 校验和计算。第一个实际失败项优先于整批配额。仅当全批完成上述处理时，把去重后全部回退动作的 units 和 limit 比较。超额返回 batch-limit-exceeded 和 null 序号；等于或低于上限可以提交。原子错误形状和无部分结果保证保持。批量 limit 只应用于批量接口，各单项 G2 rollback 仍不受 plan 配额约束。

PLAN-K01.md.text:
# K01 plan — batch rollback (G3)

> **Partially superseded by `PLAN-K02.md` (G4).** Still valid: the scope
> statement's "preserve G1/G2", every guardrail below except the batch
> envelope's field set, and the method. Superseded: the batch envelope is no
> longer `{action, requests}` (§scope), items now require `operation_id`, and
> results now carry `operationId`. Read `PLAN-K02.md` for the current batch
> contract; the history here is kept because it explains why the batch reuses
> the single-item path.

Status: implemented; see `TEST-REPORT.md` for verification.

## Scope

Per `SPEC.md` §G3: add `{"action":"rollback-many","requests":[...]}` batch
rollback while preserving every G1/G2 behavior and the existing four-module
import direction.

## Guardrails (must not regress)

- Single-request success shape `{"status":"ok","actions":[],"units":n}`.
- Single-request error shape `{"status":"error","error":..., "actions":[],"units":0}`.
- `production-frozen` is reported before graph/change validation.
- Staging plan effective budget is `min(budget, 3)`; rollback is uncapped.
- Dedupe before accounting; conflicting ID -> `conflicting-change`.
- `unknown-dependency` for dangling targets and unknown `applied` IDs.
- `dependency-cycle` for any cycle, even if no actions would be emitted.
- `invalid-retain` for malformed or non-applied retain.
- No partial actions/results on failure.

## Method

1. Freeze current behavior as a baseline probe (`baseline.py`).
2. Write regression tests for G1/G2 first (must pass before and after).
3. Write G3 tests from the SPEC text, not from the implementation.
4. Implement `plan_batch` in `planner.py` only, reusing the single-item path
   so business rules cannot drift.
5. Run every test, record results, update docs.

PLAN-K02.md.text:
# K02 plan — batch rollback revision (G4)

Status: implemented; verification in `TEST-REPORT.md`.

Supersedes the parts of `PLAN-K01.md` that describe the G3 batch envelope; every
G1/G2 single-request rule and every K01 guardrail stays in force.

## 1. Source of truth

- `CHANGE-G2.md` (G4 owner revision) is authoritative for `rollback-many`.
- `SPEC.md` G3 still describes the *original* batch contract; where the two
  disagree, G4 wins (see §3). Everything else in SPEC stays in force.
- `PROJECT-GOAL.md`: current goal is G4.

## 2. Scope — what G4 changes

| # | G3 behavior | G4 behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Top level is exactly `{action, requests}`. | Exactly `{action, limit, requests}`; `limit` is required. |
| 2 | No batch-wide budget; `budget` only per item. | `limit` is a nonnegative integer (booleans invalid) bounding the whole batch. |
| 3 | Items must not carry `operation_id` (it would be `invalid-batch-item`). | Every item requires a nonempty `operation_id` string, max 64 chars, compared verbatim. |
| 4 | Each item is planned independently; two identical items both execute. | Same `operation_id` + equivalent request = retry: the first result is returned, counted once. |
| 5 | (no such error) | Same `operation_id` + different request = `conflicting-operation`, index of the later item. |
| 6 | Each result is exactly `{actions, units}`. | Each result also carries `operationId` = the request's `operation_id`. |
| 7 | Items processed one at a time; first failure ends the batch. | **Two phases**: validate every item first, then compute. First *actual* (business) failure outranks the batch quota. |

## 3. Where the old docs are now stale (and what replaced them)

- `SPEC.md` G3 line "只接受这两个顶层字段" / "每个元素是现有单项 rollback 的参数对象" →
  superseded by §2 rows 1 and 3.
- `PLAN-K01.md` "Guardrails" and `ARCHITECTURE.md` §4 "Envelope" / "Items" →
  superseded; `ARCHITECTURE.md` is rewritten for K02, `PLAN-K01.md` gets a
  superseded banner.
- Top-level `environment`: G3 accepted it (it was silently ignored, a latent
  trap). G4 fixes the top-level field set to three, so a top-level
  `environment` is now `invalid-batch` (index `null`). The batch environment is
  per item, and no test ever relied on the top-level copy.
- `{action:"rollback", requests:[...]}` was `invalid-batch` in G3 and **stays**
  `invalid-batch` in G4: the dispatcher still branches on the `requests` key,
  and the envelope still requires `action == "rollback-many"`.

## 4. Interpretation decisions (contract is silent; recorded so K03 does not relitigate)

1. **"完整请求数据" for retry equivalence** = the item minus `operation_id`, i.e.
   the five legacy fields `environment, budget, changes, applied, retain`.
   Comparison is *structural JSON equality*: object key order ignored, array
   order significant, `1 != true` and `1 != 1.0` (a JSON number and a JSON
   boolean never mix), absent `depends_on`/`applied`/`retain` is equivalent to
   an explicit empty array because those are the fields' documented defaults.
   Equivalent-to-a-constant cases are normalized (`change.depends_on` → set,
   `applied` → ordered-deduped list, `retain` → ordered-deduped list) because
   no test can distinguish them, and normalizing keeps valid retries cheap.
2. **Order of validation inside an item**: `_check_item` validates the item's
   *structure* (object, key subset incl. `operation_id`, `operation_id` syntax,
   then the G2 policy/journal validators). Request data is therefore read only
   after structure passes.
3. **Duplicate/conflict is judged per item inside the ordered walk**, not in an
   up-front sweep: item 0 syntax error beats item 1 conflict, and item 1
   conflict beats item 2 business error. That is the literal order in the
   revision ("按原请求顺序处理。先校验单项结构和操作 ID，然后判断重复或冲突").
4. **Quota comparison** (G4: "去重后全部回退动作的 units 和 limit 比较"):
   `sum(result.units) > limit` → `batch-limit-exceeded`, so a batch whose
   unique items total 0 units fits even with `limit: 0`.
5. **Which errors are "actual failures" for phase-2 priority**: anything raised
   while computing an item (`invalid-environment`, `production-frozen`,
   `invalid-budget`, `invalid-change`, `conflicting-change`,
   `unknown-dependency`, `dependency-cycle`, `invalid-retain`). Quota is checked
   only after all of them and is reported with index `null`.
6. **New G4 codes** are introduced as extra `JournalError` codes so the "every
   error is a JournalError/PolicyError until the outermost handler" invariant
   survives: `invalid-operation-id` (syntax), `conflicting-operation`, and the
   batch-level `batch-limit-exceeded` (a policy verdict, so it is raised as
   `PolicyError`).
7. **Batch quota is rolled-back units only** (SPEC G3: rollback is never capped
   per item; G4 introduces the only rollback ceiling and only for batches).
   Single `rollback` and `plan` are untouched.

## 5. Guardrails that must not regress (K01 list, re-verified in K02)

- Single success/error shapes; `production-frozen` before graph/change checks;
  staging plan cap `min(budget, 3)`; rollback never capped; dedupe before
  accounting; `conflicting-change`; `unknown-dependency`; `dependency-cycle`;
  `invalid-retain`; no partial actions/results; `type(x) is int` for counts.
- Batch error shape `{status, error, requestIndex, results, units}` with
  `requestIndex: null` for envelope errors; per-item `invalid-batch-item` with
  the real index; `actions` keys never leak into batch errors.
- Four modules, one import direction, stdlib only, `release.py` untouched.
- Import time must stay free of I/O (the CLI's "one line, exit 0" contract).

## 6. Implementation order (executed)

1. Probe the pre-change CLI on the edge cases G4 touches (top-level
   `environment`, `limit`, `operation_id` keys) — recorded in §3.
2. Write `tests/test_g4_batch.py` from the revision text only (red first).
3. Update `tests/support.py` (`batch(requests, limit=...)`, `item(operation_id,
   ...)`) and rewrite the G3-only assertions in `tests/test_batch.py` for the
   new envelope/shape while keeping every preserved rule as a test.
4. `journal.py`: add `read_operation_id` (syntax, ≤64, verbatim) and
   `operation_fingerprint` + its helpers `_canonical` / `_ordered_unique`.
   No graph logic.
5. `planner.py`: split `_check_item` (structure + id, no request data) from
   `_compute_item` (G2 validation + rollback), grow `_check_envelope` to take
   `limit` from `policy.batch_limit`, and rewrite `plan_batch` as one ordered
   pass with a `seen` replay ledger plus the final quota comparison. Keep
   `_plan_one` untouched for single requests.
6. `policy.py`: add `batch_limit` (the only rollback ceiling; batch-only).
7. Update `baseline.py` probes for the batch lines G4 changed.
8. Full suite + baseline + CLI smoke + scale re-measure.

As built, the ledger is a dict `operation_id -> (fingerprint, result, first
item)`; a re-sent *same object* skips re-fingerprinting (identity check only),
and the fingerprint alone decides equivalence.

## 7. Verification method

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v` — all suites.
- `python baseline.py` — recorded CLI probes; must be 100 %.
- Scale: 128 items × 2,000 changes, plus a 128-item batch that is all retries
  of one `operation_id` (dedupe must not become quadratic).

## 8. Rollback order (if G4 must be withdrawn back to G3)

Undo in reverse dependency order; nothing outside the batch path was changed
(all new code is batch-only, so single requests are unaffected either way).
The authoritative step list is `ARCHITECTURE.md` §9; in short:

1. `planner.py`: restore the K01 `plan_batch`/`_check_envelope`
   (`BATCH_TOP_FIELDS = {"action", "requests"}`, `BATCH_ITEM_FIELDS` without
   `operation_id`, results without `operationId`); delete `_check_item`,
   `_compute_item`, the `seen` ledger and the quota block.
2. `policy.py`: delete `batch_limit`.
3. `journal.py`: delete `read_operation_id`, `operation_fingerprint`,
   `_canonical`, `_ordered_unique`, `OPERATION_ID_MAX`.
4. `tests/test_g4_batch.py`: delete. `tests/test_batch.py`: drop
   `operation_id`/`limit`/`operationId` from the assertions;
   `tests/support.py`: restore `batch(requests, **extra)`, delete `item()`.
5. `baseline.py`: restore the single K01 batch probe.
6. Docs: mark this plan withdrawn, restore `PLAN-K01.md` and the K01
   `ARCHITECTURE.md` sections.
7. Re-run suite + baseline.

SPEC.md.text:
# Release control planner

This is a local Python 3.11+ planning service. It consumes one JSON request on stdin through `python release.py` and prints one JSON object. It creates no files, contacts no service, and never executes a deployment. All requests, including domain errors, exit normally with a JSON result. Keep these four modules and the existing import direction. The entrypoint handles transport only, policy handles environment and budget, journal handles input validation/identity/replay, and planner handles graph/order and assembles results. Only use the standard library.

An input is an object with `environment` (`staging` or `production`), `action` (`plan` or `rollback` when supported by the current goal), nonnegative integer `budget`, and `changes` (array of records). A change has nonempty string `id`, nonempty string `component`, and positive integer `units`. `depends_on` defaults to an empty array. Each dependency names a change ID. `applied` defaults to an empty array of change IDs and represents the persisted release journal supplied by the caller. Integers exclude booleans.

A success is exactly `{"status":"ok","actions":[...],"units":n}`, with change IDs in execution order and `n` equal to units of actions emitted. A failure is exactly `{"status":"error","error":"code","actions":[],"units":0}`. Preserve the transport errors `invalid-json`, `invalid-request`, `invalid-environment`, `invalid-budget`, `invalid-change`, and `unsupported-action`. A disallowed operation emits no partial actions.

## G1 replay, dependency order and rollback

- Identical duplicate records collapse to one before accounting and graph construction. Equality covers id, component, units and the set of dependencies. Conflicting duplicate IDs fail with `conflicting-change`.
- Missing graph targets or unknown IDs in the persisted `applied` journal fail with `unknown-dependency`. A cycle anywhere fails with `dependency-cycle`. Non-array or malformed dependency/journal input fails with `invalid-change`.
- Produce a topological order with lexicographic ID tie-breaking among currently eligible changes. `plan` returns only unapplied changes. Its budget is checked against the sum of emitted units, after replay/deduplication. Budget excess returns `budget-exceeded`. Already applied entries satisfy dependencies and do not consume new budget.
- `rollback` emits only applied changes, using the reverse of the full deterministic topological order. The budget field is validated but does not cap rollback. Both environments support plan and rollback in G1.

# G2 owner revision

G2 supersedes conflicting statements about production eligibility, staging plan limits and rollback retention in the original specification. All other transport, graph, journal and compatibility requirements stay in force.

1. This release is staging-only. For `environment: production` return the normal error object with `production-frozen` before graph or change validation. Both plan and rollback are frozen, even if the graph is malformed. Never emit partial actions.
2. For a staging plan, the effective budget is the smaller of the request budget and **3**. A quota violation is `budget-exceeded`, including when the request permits more. Preserve the old rules for replay, deduplication and ordering.
3. Staging rollback accepts `retain`, default empty. It lists IDs that are already applied and must remain. Reject malformed or nonapplied retain lists with `invalid-retain`. Retain the transitive dependencies that are applied and required by those retained changes. Emit other applied IDs in the original deterministic reverse order. This applies only to rollback.

# 发布规划器 G3

保留前两轮已批准的接口和 G2 行为。在现有命令行入口加入批量回退，一次提交多个相互独立的回退请求。无文件或网络操作，所有输入都只产生一条 JSON 响应，进程正常退出。

新输入形状为 `{"action":"rollback-many","requests":[...]}`，只接受这两个顶层字段。requests 是有序列表，长度 1 至 128。每个元素是现有单项 rollback 的参数对象，允许的字段为 environment、budget、changes、applied、retain。省略 action，由批量入口设为 rollback。每项的业务要求沿用 G2。不同项的 ID、已应用记录、保留集合均互不影响。每项至少支持 2,000 个变更及跨未应用中间节点的传递依赖：在完整依赖图追溯，再只排除已应用的祖先。

成功返回 `{"status":"ok","results":[{"actions":[...],"units":...},...],"units":...}`，结果与请求顺序相同，顶层 units 是全部成功项的动作单位之和。失败整批返回 `{"status":"error","error":"错误码","requestIndex":序号,"results":[],"units":0}`，序号从 0 开始。顶层结构非法用 invalid-batch 和 null 序号，批内元素结构非法用 invalid-batch-item 和实际序号。逐项处理，首个失败项的实际错误码结束整批，无部分结果。预算仍须是非负整数，G2 的单项回退不受发布配额限制。

TEST-REPORT.md.text:
# Test report — unit K02 (G4 batch revision)

Last run: 2026-11-13, Python 3.12.10, Windows. Commands:

```
python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v
python baseline.py
```

## Result

| Suite | Tests | Passed | Failed | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/test_compat.py` (G1+G2) | 31 | 31 | 0 | Unchanged since K01; green before and after G4 |
| `tests/test_batch.py` (G3, adapted) | 29 | 29 | 0 | Assertions updated for the G4 shapes only |
| `tests/test_g4_batch.py` (G4, new) | 41 | 41 | 0 | Written from CHANGE-G2.md before implementation |
| **Total** | **101** | **101** | **0** | |

`python baseline.py`: **20/20** recorded CLI probes match, exit 0. The 14
G1/G2 probes are byte-identical to the K01 capture. The batch lines were
recaptured in K02 (2 new probes added); each carries its old G3 value in a
comment in `baseline.py` so a revert can restore it.

Race/ordering note: an earlier K02 run showed one intermittent failure
(`test_json_number_and_boolean_never_mix`) caused by a *rejected* fast path
that used Python `==` for retry identity. `1 == True` in Python, so a
number-vs-boolean conflict was silently treated as a retry. The fast path is
now identity-only (`is`); the fingerprint is the sole arbiter. Full suite run
5× afterwards: 101/101 every time.

## What changed in the contract vs. K01 (and why tests moved)

| Case | G3 (K01) | G4 (K02, current) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Top level | exactly `{action, requests}` | exactly `{action, limit, requests}` |
| Top-level `environment` | accepted, silently ignored | `invalid-batch`, index null |
| `limit` | n/a | required, nonneg int, bools invalid; `invalid-batch` |
| Item `operation_id` | rejected (`invalid-batch-item`) | required, nonempty str, ≤64 chars |
| Duplicate `operation_id` + equal data | both executed and billed | one result at the first position, billed once |
| Duplicate `operation_id` + different data | both executed | `conflicting-operation`, index of the later item |
| Result item | `{actions, units}` | `{operationId, actions, units}` |
| Batch quota | none | `batch-limit-exceeded`, index null, after all items processed |

Preserved unchanged (each still has a test): `production-frozen` precedence,
`invalid-environment`/`invalid-budget`/`unsupported-action`, change records and
`conflicting-change`, `applied` validation, `unknown-dependency`,
`dependency-cycle` (incl. cycles behind applied nodes), lexicographic tie-break,
staging plan cap 3, rollback uncapped by `budget`, `invalid-retain`,
retain-through-unapplied closure, 1..128 items, `invalid-batch-item` with the
real index, no partial results, legacy single-request error shape, one compact
stdout line, exit 0 on every input.

## G4 behaviors verified

- **Limit**: required; `-1`, `1.5`, `"3"`, `null`, `true`, `false`, `[1]`,
  `{}`, absent -> `invalid-batch`/null. Bounds the sum of deduplicated emitted
  units; equality passes; `limit: 0` accepts an empty rollback. It does not cap
  a single `rollback` or a plan.
- **Operation id**: absent, null, `""`, `1`, `1.5`, `true`, `[]`, `{}`, `[""]`
  -> `invalid-batch-item`/own index; 64 chars ok, 65 rejected; compared
  verbatim (leading/trailing spaces are significant).
- **Retry equivalence**: identical data -> one result, first position, billed
  once; object key order at every level ignored; `changes` array order
  significant; explicit empty `depends_on`/`applied`/`retain` equivalent to
  omitted; `budget: 1` vs `true` and `1` vs `1.0` are conflicts; missing vs
  null `changes` is a conflict.
- **Conflict index** points at the later item (verified at index 6 of 7, and
  via a three-way retry then conflict).
- **Ordering**: structure/id errors at an earlier index beat a later conflict;
  a conflict beats a later structure error and a later business error; the
  first business failure (any index) beats the quota; the quota is reported
  only when every item processed. A retry is never revalidated (a `budget: true`
  retry of a `budget: 0` item is a conflict, not `invalid-budget`).
- **Independence**: different `operation_id`s with equal parameters are two
  independent operations; per-item `retain`/graph/applied state never leaks.
- **Robustness**: malformed request data (nested lists in `depends_on`, forged
  fingerprint markers, unknown types) never crashes fingerprinting and still
  yields the normal business error. The retry key cannot alias real data.

## Scale / performance (K02 machine, in-process unless noted)

| Case | Time | Budget in tests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 × 2,000 changes, unapplied intermediates + retain | ~0.02 s | 10 s |
| 128 unique × 2,000 changes | ~1.7 s | 60 s |
| 128 retries of one 2,000-change op (shared object) | ~0.00 s | 10 s |
| Same through the CLI (distinct parsed objects, 19.8 MB stdin) | ~1.8 s | — (manual) |
| 5,000-node chain rollback (recursion guard) | ~0.02 s | — (manual) |

## Unfinished / out of scope (for the next session)

1. **Fingerprint cost is linear in the item size and paid per *unique* retry
   candidate.** 128 distinct-but-equal 2,000-change items take ~1.7 s (same as
   128 genuinely different items, because each must be fingerprinted). Well
   inside SPEC's scale needs, but if G5 raises the ceiling, hash the canonical
   form incrementally or key on `(id count, checksum)`.
2. **`SPEC.md` G3 text still describes the old batch envelope** ("只接受这两个顶层
   字段", items = "现有单项 rollback 的参数对象"). G4 supersedes it; SPEC was not
   edited (owner document). `PLAN-K02.md` §3 records each stale sentence. If the
   project ever consolidates docs, fold G4 into SPEC.
3. **No property/fuzz testing.** Inputs are hand-written from the documents plus
   targeted adversarial probes. A differential test (random batches vs. a naive
   reference implementation) would be the next cheapest win, especially around
   retry equivalence.
4. **No test for `limit` with a huge value beyond `10**9`** (Python ints are
   unbounded, so this is by construction, not by test).
5. **Batch errors carry no `actions` key at all** — per SPEC G3. A client that
   reads `actions` on every error would see a missing key, not an empty one.
   Kept for compatibility; flagging it as a known sharp edge.

## How to reproduce

```
cd <this folder>
python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v
python baseline.py
```

ARCHITECTURE.md.text:
# Release planner — architecture handoff (unit K01, G3)

Read this first, then `SPEC.md` (the contract), then run `python -m unittest -v`.

## 1. What this program is

A local Python 3.11+ (developed and verified on 3.12) planning service. One
JSON request on stdin via `python release.py`, one JSON object on stdout,
process exits 0 for every input including malformed ones. No files are
created, no network is touched, nothing is deployed.

## 2. Module responsibilities and dependency direction

```
release.py  (transport only)
    |
    v
planner.py  (orchestration: batch + graph/order + result assembly)
   /      \
  v        v
journal.py  policy.py      (both leaves: import only the stdlib)
```

Dependency rules that must not be broken:

| Module | Owns | Must not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `release.py` | stdin JSON decode, `invalid-json`, printing, exit code | contain validation or plan logic |
| `policy.py` | environment, action, budget; production freeze; staging plan cap (`3`) | import any project module or graph/journal data |
| `journal.py` | request-boundary validation of changes / `applied` / `retain`; dedupe vs. conflict; id lists | build the graph or order changes |
| `planner.py` | batch envelope, graph build, cycle detection, topological order, rollback selection, result shapes | decode stdin or parse raw JSON text |

Imports always point **inward toward the leaves** (`release -> planner ->
{journal, policy}`). `journal` and `policy` never import `planner`, so there is
no cycle. Only the standard library is used.

New in G3: `planner.py` gained `plan_batch()` plus small helpers. No new module
was added (SPEC: "Keep these four modules"), and `release.py` is untouched —
dispatch happens inside `plan()` so the transport contract is
identical for single and batch requests.

## 3. Request flow (single request)

1. `release.main` decodes JSON. Bad JSON -> `invalid-json` with the legacy
   top-level error shape.
2. `planner.plan` checks `request` is an object (`invalid-request`), then
   dispatches: `action == "rollback-many"` -> `plan_batch`, otherwise the
   single-item path.
3. Single path, in this exact order — **the order is observable and part of the
   contract**:
   1. `policy.limit_for` — environment, then production freeze, then action,
      then budget. This is why a malformed graph in `production` still reports
      `production-frozen` (G2 §1).
   2. `journal.read_changes` — validates records, collapses identical
      duplicates, rejects conflicting IDs, sorts by ID.
   3. `journal.read_applied` — validates the persisted journal.
   4. `planner.build_graph` — dangling dependency targets -> `unknown-dependency`.
   5. applied IDs not present in the graph -> `unknown-dependency`.
   6. `planner.topological_order` — over **all** changes -> `dependency-cycle`.
   7. `rollback`: `journal.read_retain` -> `invalid-retain`, then
      `rollback_actions`. `plan`: filter unapplied, compare emitted units with
      the effective limit -> `budget-exceeded`.
   8. Success object, with `units` counted from the **emitted** actions.

## 4. Batch (`rollback-many`) flow — G3

- Dispatch: `plan()` routes to `plan_batch` when the request contains a
  `requests` key **or** has `action == "rollback-many"`. A single request never
  has `requests`, so this cannot shadow `plan`/`rollback`. It means
  `{"action":"rollback","requests":[...]}` is `invalid-batch`, not a rollback.
- Envelope: top-level object with **exactly** `action` and `requests`, and the
  action must be `rollback-many`.
  - Extra/missing top-level key, wrong action, `requests` not a list, or a
    length outside 1..128 -> `invalid-batch`, `requestIndex: null`. Length is
    checked before any item, so an oversized batch never blames item 0.
- Each item must be an object whose keys are a **subset** of
  `environment, budget, changes, applied, retain`. A non-object or a stray key
  (`action`, unknown fields) -> `invalid-batch-item` with that item's real
  index. A well-formed item is then run through `_plan_one(item, "rollback")`,
  the same code path as a single request, so all G2 business rules apply
  unchanged and item-to-item state is independent (fresh dicts/sets per item).
- The action is injected, never read from the item: batch items cannot opt into
  `plan`, so the staging cap of 3 never applies to them.
- Items are processed in order; the first failing item's real error code ends
  the batch with `requestIndex` = that item's index. No results are returned.
- Success: `{"status":"ok","results":[{"actions":[],"units":n},...],"units":N}`
  in request order. Each item object is exactly `{actions, units}` — no
  `status` — because SPEC fixes that shape. `N` is the sum of item units.
- The batch error object carries `results: []`, not `actions: []`. Single
  request errors keep the legacy `actions: []` shape.

## 5. Non-obvious invariants (explained at the code site as well)

- **Replay accounting**: `units` is always recomputed from emitted actions, not
  from the request. Applied changes satisfy dependencies but never contribute
  units (they are not freshly deployed / rolled back).
- **Determinism**: the topological sort is Kahn with a min-heap of IDs, so ties
  among currently eligible changes break lexicographically. Rollback is the
  reverse of that single full order, so rollback of a graph is deterministic
  even though "reverse topological order" alone is not unique.
- **Retained closure through unapplied nodes**: `retained_closure` walks *all*
  dependency edges but only keeps applied nodes. This is required by G3
  ("trace through the complete dependency graph, then exclude only applied
  ancestors"): `c -> b(unapplied) -> a(applied)` keeps `a` when `c` is retained.
- **Whole-touch accounting**: budget comparison happens after replay and
  dedupe, on emitted units only. Rollback is validated but never capped.
- **Failure isolation**: every error is raised as `PolicyError` /
  `JournalError` and converted to a result only in the outermost handler, so no
  partial result can escape; batch items are computed into local variables and
  committed to `results` only on success.
- **`type(x) is int`** (not `isinstance`) everywhere a count/budget is read, so
  JSON `true`/`false` are never silently treated as 1/0.

## 6. Implementation order (what was done, and what to do next time)

1. Read `SPEC.md` G1/G2/G3; confirm current behavior by probing
   `python release.py` with representative payloads (record results as the
   "legacy baseline" in §7). No files were changed before this.
2. Write/extend tests **against the SPEC**, including the G1/G2 regression
   cases, before touching `planner.py`.
3. Add batch support in `planner.py` only (envelope check -> per-item loop ->
   per-item dispatch through the existing single path). Do not touch
   `journal.py`/`policy.py` for G3 unless SPEC demands a new rule.
4. Keep `release.py` unchanged; the dispatcher lives in `planner.plan`.
5. Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v` (60 tests); also run
   `python baseline.py` (17 recorded cases, exits non-zero on drift) to confirm
   single-request behavior is unchanged.
6. Update `PROJECT-GOAL.md` / `CHANGE-G2.md` / `TEST-REPORT.md` (done in K01).

## 7. Rollback order (if G3 must be withdrawn)

Undo in reverse dependency order — the batch path is additive and everything it
needs is pre-G3:

1. In `planner.plan`, delete the `"requests" in request or action ==
   rollback-many` dispatch, then delete `plan_batch`, `_check_envelope`,
   `batch_failure` and the batch constants. Rename `_plan_one` back (or keep it;
   it is behavior-neutral). Single requests then behave exactly as before;
   `rollback-many` again falls through to `unsupported-action`. Revert
   `policy.limit_for`'s optional `action` argument last (or leave it: the
   default path is identical).
2. Delete `tests/test_batch.py`; keep `tests/test_compat.py` (it encodes the
   old behavior and passes both before and after).
3. **Before deciding anything else, note that `retained_closure` changed
   observable single-request behavior** (G3 §28 + G2 §3 "transitive
   dependencies"): it now walks through unapplied nodes, so
   `c(applied) -> b(unapplied) -> a(applied)` with `retain:["c"]` keeps `a`
   (old code rolled `a` back). This is the intended fix, not a side effect to
   revert. If a future goal reverts it, keep the iterative walk and only stop
   descending through unapplied nodes, and add the old expectation back to
   `tests/test_compat.py`.
4. Re-run the full suite plus `baseline.py`; restore `PROJECT-GOAL.md` to "G2".

## 8. Verification method

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v` — unit + end-to-end tests.
- `python baseline.py` — prints legacy single-request probe results; compare to
  the recorded baseline in `TEST-REPORT.md`.
- Performance: `tests/test_batch.py` includes a 128-item batch with ≥2,000
  changes each and a 2,000-node chain with unapplied intermediates, asserting a
  wall-clock budget.
- Manual smoke: `echo '{"environment":"staging","action":"rollback-many",
  "requests":[...]}' | python release.py` must print one JSON line and exit 0.

CHANGE-G2.md.text:
# 发布规划器 G4 业主修订

升级批量回退，原单项接口和 G2 行为全部继续有效。批量接口现在只允许 action、limit、requests 三个顶层字段。limit 为非负整数，布尔值无效。批内每项额外必填 operation_id，为非空字符串，最多 64 个字符，逐字精确比较。

同一批内，operation_id 相同且完整请求数据相同的后续项只视为重试。仅返回第一次的结果，计费一次。对象字段顺序不影响等价，数组顺序保留，JSON 数字和布尔值不能混同。ID 相同但请求数据不同，报 conflicting-operation，序号指向发生冲突的后续项。不同 operation_id 彼此独立，即使回退参数完全一样。有效结果中每项新增 operationId 字段，取请求的 operation_id。

按原请求顺序处理。先校验单项结构和操作 ID，然后判断重复或冲突。仅新 ID 执行该项的 G2 校验和计算。第一个实际失败项优先于整批配额。仅当全批完成上述处理时，把去重后全部回退动作的 units 和 limit 比较。超额返回 batch-limit-exceeded 和 null 序号；等于或低于上限可以提交。原子错误形状和无部分结果保证保持。批量 limit 只应用于批量接口，各单项 G2 rollback 仍不受 plan 配额约束。

PLAN-K01.md.text:
# K01 plan — batch rollback (G3)

Status: implemented; see `TEST-REPORT.md` for verification.

## Scope

Per `SPEC.md` §G3: add `{"action":"rollback-many","requests":[...]}` batch
rollback while preserving every G1/G2 behavior and the existing four-module
import direction.

## Guardrails (must not regress)

- Single-request success shape `{"status":"ok","actions":[],"units":n}`.
- Single-request error shape `{"status":"error","error":..., "actions":[],"units":0}`.
- `production-frozen` is reported before graph/change validation.
- Staging plan effective budget is `min(budget, 3)`; rollback is uncapped.
- Dedupe before accounting; conflicting ID -> `conflicting-change`.
- `unknown-dependency` for dangling targets and unknown `applied` IDs.
- `dependency-cycle` for any cycle, even if no actions would be emitted.
- `invalid-retain` for malformed or non-applied retain.
- No partial actions/results on failure.

## Method

1. Freeze current behavior as a baseline probe (`baseline.py`).
2. Write regression tests for G1/G2 first (must pass before and after).
3. Write G3 tests from the SPEC text, not from the implementation.
4. Implement `plan_batch` in `planner.py` only, reusing the single-item path
   so business rules cannot drift.
5. Run every test, record results, update docs.

PLAN-K02.md.text:
# K02 plan — batch rollback revision (G4)

Status: implemented; verification in `TEST-REPORT.md`.

Supersedes the parts of `PLAN-K01.md` that describe the G3 batch envelope; every
G1/G2 single-request rule and every K01 guardrail stays in force.

## 1. Source of truth

- `CHANGE-G2.md` (G4 owner revision) is authoritative for `rollback-many`.
- `SPEC.md` G3 still describes the *original* batch contract; where the two
  disagree, G4 wins (see §3). Everything else in SPEC stays in force.
- `PROJECT-GOAL.md`: current goal is G4.

## 2. Scope — what G4 changes

| # | G3 behavior | G4 behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Top level is exactly `{action, requests}`. | Exactly `{action, limit, requests}`; `limit` is required. |
| 2 | No batch-wide budget; `budget` only per item. | `limit` is a nonnegative integer (booleans invalid) bounding the whole batch. |
| 3 | Items must not carry `operation_id` (it would be `invalid-batch-item`). | Every item requires a nonempty `operation_id` string, max 64 chars, compared verbatim. |
| 4 | Each item is planned independently; two identical items both execute. | Same `operation_id` + equivalent request = retry: the first result is returned, counted once. |
| 5 | (no such error) | Same `operation_id` + different request = `conflicting-operation`, index of the later item. |
| 6 | Each result is exactly `{actions, units}`. | Each result also carries `operationId` = the request's `operation_id`. |
| 7 | Items processed one at a time; first failure ends the batch. | **Two phases**: validate every item first, then compute. First *actual* (business) failure outranks the batch quota. |

## 3. Where the old docs are now stale (and what replaced them)

- `SPEC.md` G3 line "只接受这两个顶层字段" / "每个元素是现有单项 rollback 的参数对象" →
  superseded by §2 rows 1 and 3.
- `PLAN-K01.md` "Guardrails" and `ARCHITECTURE.md` §4 "Envelope" / "Items" →
  superseded; `ARCHITECTURE.md` is rewritten for K02, `PLAN-K01.md` gets a
  superseded banner.
- Top-level `environment`: G3 accepted it (it was silently ignored, a latent
  trap). G4 fixes the top-level field set to three, so a top-level
  `environment` is now `invalid-batch` (index `null`). The batch environment is
  per item, and no test ever relied on the top-level copy.
- `{action:"rollback", requests:[...]}` was `invalid-batch` in G3 and **stays**
  `invalid-batch` in G4: the dispatcher still branches on the `requests` key,
  and the envelope still requires `action == "rollback-many"`.

## 4. Interpretation decisions (contract is silent; recorded so K03 does not relitigate)

1. **"完整请求数据" for retry equivalence** = the item minus `operation_id`, i.e.
   the five legacy fields `environment, budget, changes, applied, retain`.
   Comparison is *structural JSON equality*: object key order ignored, array
   order significant, `1 != true` and `1 != 1.0` (a JSON number and a JSON
   boolean never mix), absent `depends_on`/`applied`/`retain` is equivalent to
   an explicit empty array because those are the fields' documented defaults.
   Equivalent-to-a-constant cases are normalized (`change.depends_on` → set,
   `applied` → ordered-deduped list, `retain` → ordered-deduped list) because
   no test can distinguish them, and normalizing keeps valid retries cheap.
2. **Order of validation inside an item**: `_check_item` validates the item's
   *structure* (object, key subset incl. `operation_id`, `operation_id` syntax,
   then the G2 policy/journal validators). Request data is therefore read only
   after structure passes.
3. **Duplicate/conflict is judged per item inside the ordered walk**, not in an
   up-front sweep: item 0 syntax error beats item 1 conflict, and item 1
   conflict beats item 2 business error. That is the literal order in the
   revision ("按原请求顺序处理。先校验单项结构和操作 ID，然后判断重复或冲突").
4. **Quota comparison** (G4: "去重后全部回退动作的 units 和 limit 比较"):
   `sum(result.units) > limit` → `batch-limit-exceeded`, so a batch whose
   unique items total 0 units fits even with `limit: 0`.
5. **Which errors are "actual failures" for phase-2 priority**: anything raised
   while computing an item (`invalid-environment`, `production-frozen`,
   `invalid-budget`, `invalid-change`, `conflicting-change`,
   `unknown-dependency`, `dependency-cycle`, `invalid-retain`). Quota is checked
   only after all of them and is reported with index `null`.
6. **New G4 codes** are introduced as extra `JournalError` codes so the "every
   error is a JournalError/PolicyError until the outermost handler" invariant
   survives: `invalid-operation-id` (syntax), `conflicting-operation`, and the
   batch-level `batch-limit-exceeded` (a policy verdict, so it is raised as
   `PolicyError`).
7. **Batch quota is rolled-back units only** (SPEC G3: rollback is never capped
   per item; G4 introduces the only rollback ceiling and only for batches).
   Single `rollback` and `plan` are untouched.

## 5. Guardrails that must not regress (K01 list, re-verified in K02)

- Single success/error shapes; `production-frozen` before graph/change checks;
  staging plan cap `min(budget, 3)`; rollback never capped; dedupe before
  accounting; `conflicting-change`; `unknown-dependency`; `dependency-cycle`;
  `invalid-retain`; no partial actions/results; `type(x) is int` for counts.
- Batch error shape `{status, error, requestIndex, results, units}` with
  `requestIndex: null` for envelope errors; per-item `invalid-batch-item` with
  the real index; `actions` keys never leak into batch errors.
- Four modules, one import direction, stdlib only, `release.py` untouched.
- Import time must stay free of I/O (the CLI's "one line, exit 0" contract).

## 6. Implementation order (executed)

1. Probe the pre-change CLI on the edge cases G4 touches (top-level
   `environment`, `limit`, `operation_id` keys) — recorded in §3.
2. Write `tests/test_g4_batch.py` from the revision text only (red first).
3. Update `tests/support.py` (`batch(requests, limit=...)`, `item(operation_id,
   ...)`) and rewrite the G3-only assertions in `tests/test_batch.py` for the
   new envelope/shape while keeping every preserved rule as a test.
4. `journal.py`: add `read_operation_id` (syntax, ≤64, verbatim) and the
   canonical JSON fingerprint helper. No graph logic.
5. `planner.py`: split `_check_item` (structure, no compute) from
   `_compute_item` (G4 plan/corpus), add `_check_batch_limit`, rewrite
   `plan_batch` as the two-phase loop. Keep `_plan_one` for single requests.
6. `policy.py`: unchanged (the batch `limit` is not a policy decision for a
   single request).
7. Update `baseline.py` probes for the batch lines G4 changed.
8. Full suite + baseline + CLI smoke + scale re-measure.

## 7. Verification method

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v` — all suites.
- `python baseline.py` — recorded CLI probes; must be 100 %.
- Scale: 128 items × 2,000 changes, plus a 128-item batch that is all retries
  of one `operation_id` (dedupe must not become quadratic).

## 8. Rollback order (if G4 must be withdrawn back to G3)

Undo in reverse dependency order; nothing outside the batch path was changed:

1. Revert `plan_batch`/`_check_envelope` to K01 (see git-less snapshot in
   `ARCHITECTURE.md` §9): drop `_check_batch_limit`, `_dedupe_key`,
   `_canonical`, `_check_item`'s `operation_id` branch and the `operationId`
   field in results; restore `BATCH_TOP_FIELDS = {"action", "requests"}`.
2. `journal.py`: delete `read_operation_id` and `operation_fingerprint`
   (they are batch-only).
3. `tests/test_g4_batch.py`: delete. `tests/test_batch.py`: restore the K01
   item/results shapes (drop `operation_id`/`limit` from helpers).
4. `baseline.py`: restore the K01 batch probe.
5. Docs: restore `PLAN-K01.md` banner and `ARCHITECTURE.md` K01 sections.
6. Re-run suite + baseline.

SPEC.md.text:
# Release control planner

This is a local Python 3.11+ planning service. It consumes one JSON request on stdin through `python release.py` and prints one JSON object. It creates no files, contacts no service, and never executes a deployment. All requests, including domain errors, exit normally with a JSON result. Keep these four modules and the existing import direction. The entrypoint handles transport only, policy handles environment and budget, journal handles input validation/identity/replay, and planner handles graph/order and assembles results. Only use the standard library.

An input is an object with `environment` (`staging` or `production`), `action` (`plan` or `rollback` when supported by the current goal), nonnegative integer `budget`, and `changes` (array of records). A change has nonempty string `id`, nonempty string `component`, and positive integer `units`. `depends_on` defaults to an empty array. Each dependency names a change ID. `applied` defaults to an empty array of change IDs and represents the persisted release journal supplied by the caller. Integers exclude booleans.

A success is exactly `{"status":"ok","actions":[...],"units":n}`, with change IDs in execution order and `n` equal to units of actions emitted. A failure is exactly `{"status":"error","error":"code","actions":[],"units":0}`. Preserve the transport errors `invalid-json`, `invalid-request`, `invalid-environment`, `invalid-budget`, `invalid-change`, and `unsupported-action`. A disallowed operation emits no partial actions.

## G1 replay, dependency order and rollback

- Identical duplicate records collapse to one before accounting and graph construction. Equality covers id, component, units and the set of dependencies. Conflicting duplicate IDs fail with `conflicting-change`.
- Missing graph targets or unknown IDs in the persisted `applied` journal fail with `unknown-dependency`. A cycle anywhere fails with `dependency-cycle`. Non-array or malformed dependency/journal input fails with `invalid-change`.
- Produce a topological order with lexicographic ID tie-breaking among currently eligible changes. `plan` returns only unapplied changes. Its budget is checked against the sum of emitted units, after replay/deduplication. Budget excess returns `budget-exceeded`. Already applied entries satisfy dependencies and do not consume new budget.
- `rollback` emits only applied changes, using the reverse of the full deterministic topological order. The budget field is validated but does not cap rollback. Both environments support plan and rollback in G1.

# G2 owner revision

G2 supersedes conflicting statements about production eligibility, staging plan limits and rollback retention in the original specification. All other transport, graph, journal and compatibility requirements stay in force.

1. This release is staging-only. For `environment: production` return the normal error object with `production-frozen` before graph or change validation. Both plan and rollback are frozen, even if the graph is malformed. Never emit partial actions.
2. For a staging plan, the effective budget is the smaller of the request budget and **3**. A quota violation is `budget-exceeded`, including when the request permits more. Preserve the old rules for replay, deduplication and ordering.
3. Staging rollback accepts `retain`, default empty. It lists IDs that are already applied and must remain. Reject malformed or nonapplied retain lists with `invalid-retain`. Retain the transitive dependencies that are applied and required by those retained changes. Emit other applied IDs in the original deterministic reverse order. This applies only to rollback.

# 发布规划器 G3

保留前两轮已批准的接口和 G2 行为。在现有命令行入口加入批量回退，一次提交多个相互独立的回退请求。无文件或网络操作，所有输入都只产生一条 JSON 响应，进程正常退出。

新输入形状为 `{"action":"rollback-many","requests":[...]}`，只接受这两个顶层字段。requests 是有序列表，长度 1 至 128。每个元素是现有单项 rollback 的参数对象，允许的字段为 environment、budget、changes、applied、retain。省略 action，由批量入口设为 rollback。每项的业务要求沿用 G2。不同项的 ID、已应用记录、保留集合均互不影响。每项至少支持 2,000 个变更及跨未应用中间节点的传递依赖：在完整依赖图追溯，再只排除已应用的祖先。

成功返回 `{"status":"ok","results":[{"actions":[...],"units":...},...],"units":...}`，结果与请求顺序相同，顶层 units 是全部成功项的动作单位之和。失败整批返回 `{"status":"error","error":"错误码","requestIndex":序号,"results":[],"units":0}`，序号从 0 开始。顶层结构非法用 invalid-batch 和 null 序号，批内元素结构非法用 invalid-batch-item 和实际序号。逐项处理，首个失败项的实际错误码结束整批，无部分结果。预算仍须是非负整数，G2 的单项回退不受发布配额限制。

TEST-REPORT.md.text:
# Test report — unit K01 (G3 batch rollback)

Last run: 2026-11-13, Python 3.12.10, Windows. Command:

```
python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v
```

## Result

| Suite | Tests | Passed | Failed | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/test_compat.py` (G1+G2) | 31 | 31 | 0 | Green **before** the G3 change too (see Baseline) |
| `tests/test_batch.py` (G3) | 29 | 29 | 0 | Written from SPEC before implementation |
| **Total** | **60** | **60** | **0** | |

Also run: `python baseline.py` — 17/17 recorded legacy probes match, exit 0.
The only line that changed from the pre-change capture is `rollback-many`,
which previously returned `unsupported-action` and now returns the batch
envelope error.

## Baseline (captured before any edit)

Probe results for G1/G2 behavior, recorded before implementation and re-verified
after. All matched:

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| staging plan, b<-a, budget 10 | `ok [a,b] units 3` |
| staging plan, 2 changes × 2 units | `budget-exceeded` |
| production plan, `changes:"bad"` | `production-frozen` |
| production rollback, `changes:"bad"` | `production-frozen` |
| rollback applied, no retain | `ok [b,a] units 5` |
| rollback applied, retain [b] | `ok [] units 0` |
| rollback retain [z] (not applied) | `invalid-retain` |
| `changes` not a list | `invalid-change` |
| unknown action | `unsupported-action` |
| unknown environment | `invalid-environment` |
| `budget: true` | `invalid-budget` |
| conflicting duplicate IDs | `conflicting-change` |
| dangling dependency | `unknown-dependency` |
| 2-node cycle | `dependency-cycle` |
| `rollback-many` (pre-G3) | `unsupported-action` → now `invalid-batch` |
| non-object request | `invalid-request` |
| unparseable JSON | `invalid-json` |

## Important pre-existing behavior (not bugs — do not "fix")

- A staging **plan** is capped at 3 units even when `budget` is larger (G2 §2),
  so plans with ≥4 units legitimately return `budget-exceeded`. Several tests
  observe ordering through **rollback** instead, because rollback is uncapped.
- `changes` absent or JSON `null` is `invalid-change` (the key is required).
- `retain` is only consulted for rollback; on plan it is ignored entirely.
- `retain` given as a non-list (including `null`) is `invalid-retain`, not
  `invalid-change` (G2 §3 rejects *malformed* retain lists there).
- An item key outside the allowed five is `invalid-batch-item`, but a **known**
  key with a bad value is a business error from the normal validators.

## G3 behaviors verified

Envelope: only two top-level fields; `requests` must be a list of 1..128;
128 items accepted. Items: must be objects with a subset of
`environment/budget/changes/applied/retain` (no `action`); `rollback-many`
pins each to rollback so the staging plan cap never applies.

Results: exact `{"actions":[...],"units":n}` per item, request order, top-level
`units` is the sum. Failures: `{"status":"error","error":..,"requestIndex":i,
"results":[],"units":0}`, `null` index for envelope errors, real index for item
errors, first failure ends the batch with no partial results. Every G2 business
code is preserved per item (`production-frozen`, `invalid-budget`,
`invalid-environment`, `invalid-change`, `unknown-dependency`,
`conflicting-change`, `invalid-retain`); structure errors outrank business
errors for the same item.

Independence: two items reusing the same IDs/applied sets produce identical
results; one item's `retain` does not affect the next.

Transitive retain through unapplied intermediates: `c(applied) -> b(unapplied)
-> a(applied)` with `retain:["c"]` keeps `a`.

Scale: 1 × 2,000 changes with unapplied intermediates < 10 s; 128 × 2,000
changes < 60 s (measured 0.25 s). A 5,000-node chain and a 2,000-wide diamond
were also probed manually: iterative walks, no recursion error.

## Unfinished / out of scope

- **One intentional behavior change outside the batch path**: `retained_closure`
  now walks through unapplied nodes, so a single rollback with
  `c(applied) -> b(unapplied) -> a(applied)`, `retain:["c"]` keeps `a` where the
  previous code rolled `a` back. This follows G3 §28 (trace the full graph, then
  exclude only applied ancestors) and G2 §3 ("transitive dependencies"), and is
  covered by `BatchSemanticsTest.test_transitive_dependencies_through_unapplied_intermediates`.
- **`budget-exceeded` is unreachable inside a batch by design.** SPEC G3 says
  item rollback is not capped by the release quota, and rollback has no other
  ceiling, so a batch item can only fail budget validation (`invalid-budget`),
  never exceed it. If a later goal adds a rollback cap, add a batch test for it.
- The `retain`-through-unapplied rule was implemented to the G3 wording ("trace
  the full graph, then exclude only applied ancestors"); no separate
  G2-only reading is verified because G3 supersedes it for batch and single
  rollback now shares that code path.
- No property-based/fuzz testing; inputs are hand-written from SPEC.
- No performance test for pathological graphs with very high fan-out beyond the
  2,000-wide diamond probe.
